gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly identifies the abstract's universal no-PTAS claim as applying to criteria for which the paper establishes only narrower results, including the polynomial-time Frobenius case and p>2 cases without a PTAS gap. Its specific repair qualifies the abstract claim to the proved subset, matching the gold defect.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the same overbroad abstract assertion that every listed criterion lacks a PTAS, despite an exact polynomial-time Frobenius algorithm and incomplete no-PTAS results for other listed criteria.

component_coverage.gold_component: The abstract falsely universalizes the no-PTAS conclusion across all listed criteria, contradicting the polynomial-time Frobenius case and exceeding the established inapproximability scope.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction names both the polynomial-time Frobenius exception and the p>2 criteria lacking a proved PTAS gap, explains that the advertised scope exceeds the proved subset, and supplies the corresponding qualified-abstract repair.
